# Customer Onboarding Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Customer Onboarding Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 7 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded onboarding files, the proposed case, document, screening and banking connections and the channel; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for Dynamics 365 cases, the SharePoint library, identity and screening services, core banking and Teams, each with a least-privilege reference. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare specialist, relationship-manager, compliance, onboarding-head and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Decision ownership | Have the onboarding owner name who verifies identity, clears screening, approves applicants and provisions accounts before real applications replace the snapshot. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Onboarding business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Onboarding applications by status, open checks, document collection and handoffs before activation Establish where manual handoffs delay files and where check evidence is hard to prove before attributing change to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Application type | Measurement period | Status | Open checks | Documents outstanding | Owner | Handoffs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Onboarding business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Onboarding business owner | Approve onboarding scope, routing and escalation; agree production success measures before go-live. |
| Authorized onboarding and compliance reviewers | Own verification, eligibility, consent, approval and provisioning decisions that the agent only prepares. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; confirm the saved instructions, remove web search and record Draft state. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any onboarding connection is approved. |
| Onboarding connection owners | Approve Dynamics 365, SharePoint, identity and screening, core-banking and Teams access through least-privilege connection references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Close the open review gates with a fresh saved-state check, all FCO cases and personally reviewed per-step evidence. |
| Operations owner | Own production monitoring, support and configuration recovery; route verification and approval requests to authorized reviewers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for onboarding have named agreement.
- [ ] The onboarding owner records current handoffs, check evidence and document collection before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/fs-customer-onboarding/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and confirm blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The approved environment and publisher prefix for the onboarding build are recorded before a build lane is chosen.
- [ ] The customer approves the sign-in requirement, audience and least-privilege scopes for applicant identity and screening data before any connection is bound.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/fs-customer-onboarding/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/fs-customer-onboarding/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/fs-customer-onboarding/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/fs-customer-onboarding/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Customer Onboarding Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_fs-customer-onboarding-controls-and-review.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_fs-customer-onboarding-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_account-setup_02
9. Add skill: aibast_document-checklist_03
10. Add skill: aibast_kyc-verification_01
11. Add skill: aibast_onboarding-status_04
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Run and verify FCO-01: Compliance Officer
15. Run and verify FCO-02: Onboarding Specialist
16. Run and verify FCO-03: Relationship Manager
17. Run and verify FCO-04: Head of Onboarding
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: FCO-01, FCO-02, FCO-03, FCO-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Step 2-5. Close review gates

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Run a fresh live regression of the assembled package, including the changed controls knowledge, and close each open review gate.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] A fresh saved-state check confirms the instructions, two knowledge files and four skills on the current Draft.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, the smoke test calls `FSCustomerOnboardingAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] Every locked FCO case passes a fresh live regression with routing, retrieval, citation and safety evidence.
- [ ] Marker matches alone are not accepted; factual, routing, citation and safety correctness are reviewed.
- [ ] Every declared step has freshly captured or personally reviewed evidence; no current capture is reusable yet.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before any applicant identity or screening information is shown. Request only the scopes that approved case, document and screening sources need. Restrict the audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 onboarding or CRM case data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Onboarding connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 onboarding or CRM case data — read:** Bind application-scoped read-only case lookups that require an explicit ID.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 onboarding or CRM case data:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 onboarding or CRM case data:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 onboarding or CRM case data:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): No ranking, elapsed time or SLA; return the recorded status and owner pairs. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, verification or provisioning succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate SharePoint controlled-document library

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Onboarding connection owners

1. **Bind SharePoint controlled-document library — read:** Add the controlled library as knowledge with a content owner.

2. **Identity for SharePoint controlled-document library:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope SharePoint controlled-document library:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for SharePoint controlled-document library:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Infer no receipt or missing status and send nothing; beneficial_ownership is only in progress. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, verification or provisioning succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Approved identity and sanctions-screening services

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Onboarding connection owners

1. **Bind Approved identity and sanctions-screening services — read:** Expose read-only check results through an approved connector or MCP tool.

2. **Identity for Approved identity and sanctions-screening services:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved identity and sanctions-screening services:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved identity and sanctions-screening services:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Verify and clear nothing; report pep_screening as flagged, not a verified match, for compliance review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, verification or provisioning succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Core-banking provisioning workflow

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Onboarding connection owners

1. **Bind Core-banking provisioning workflow — write:** Keep provisioning in the approved workflow; any tool needs explicit authorization and an audit record (preview).

2. **Identity for Core-banking provisioning workflow:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Core-banking provisioning workflow:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Core-banking provisioning workflow:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Approve and open nothing; review-ready is not approved, consented, provisioned or opened. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, verification or provisioning succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams approvals

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Onboarding connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams approvals — write:** Gate any Teams approval card behind authorized reviewers.

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams approvals:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams approvals:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams approvals:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): No ranking, elapsed time or SLA; return the recorded status and owner pairs. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Treat it as not proof and never describe it as captured.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Onboarding connection owners

Create only approved least-privilege tools; keep identity, screening and core-banking actions behind explicit authorization gates.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Only approved least-privilege tools are bound, and consequential actions keep explicit approval gates.
- [ ] No lookup, verification, provisioning or record change is reported unless an approved production tool returns success evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test the approved deployment with onboarding and denied identities; a maker's working connection does not prove other users' access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic progress, assets and product terms are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations name the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact onboarding assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked onboarding corpus | All four cases, FCO-01 through FCO-04, return every required marker, no forbidden phrase and the minimum word count. |
| Preservation-review gates | The recorded review is blocked until a fresh live regression, saved-state check and reviewed per-step evidence close its open gates. |
| Manual inventory | Saved global instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model are confirmed, with no tools. |
| Regulated authority boundary | Any verification, clearance, approval, account opening, provisioning, outreach or record-change claim is no-go. |
| Publish safety gate | Synthetic labels, human review and no-advice, no-approval, no-transaction behavior are validated before publish. |
| Release state | Both validated agents remain Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Onboarding business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Onboarding business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation from the approval owner.
- [ ] The approved onboarding audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed sessions, wrong-application answers, connection errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Recovery is rehearsed with a restore path supported for the onboarding environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, knowledge use, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

## Deliverables Checklist

### Template provides

- [ ] Agent, synthetic data and component inventory.
- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Adapted mappings, identities, governance and connections.
- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
